claims.text: The proposed coating material is a 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 high-entropy-alloy nanoflake material.
The nanoflakes can be deposited as a uniform coating on CoCrFeNi by spray coating.
Spray-coated 2D HEA nanoflakes enable formation of a continuous, self-organized tribofilm on the wear track.
The tribofilm contains amorphous or nanocrystalline oxide and/or carbonaceous lubricious phases.
Sliding stress induces tribocatalytic activity in the HEA nanoflakes.
Tribocatalytic activity triggers dissociation of entrapped molecules and/or surface oxidation.
The resulting tribolayer is stable and has low shear strength.
The tribolayer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact, thereby lowering friction and wear.
The coating remains tribologically effective from room temperature to 800 °C.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower average coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
Reductions in both friction and wear will be statistically significant.
The lubricating mechanism remains effective as load and sliding speed vary.
The lubricating mechanism remains effective as environmental conditions vary.
The coating's long-term durability and adhesion at high temperature and varying load are uncertain.
Compatibility of the coating with changing tribochemical environments is uncertain.
Water-based HEA-nanoflake coatings can fail rapidly and exhibit wear rates around 10^-6 mm3/(N·m), compared with around 10^-9 mm3/(N·m) for ethanol-based coatings.
A controlled comparison of coated and uncoated CoCrFeNi can test the proposed friction and wear benefits.
Continuous coefficient-of-friction monitoring and 3D wear-track profilometry provide measurable outcomes for the test.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both average friction coefficient and wear rate across the full temperature range would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis states that the tribofilm will remain effective through 800 °C, while the uncertainty field says high-temperature durability, adhesion, and compatibility remain unestablished.
The mechanism claims effectiveness as environmental conditions vary, but the proposed boundary and experiment cover only dry ambient conditions and therefore do not test environmental variation.
The design refers to wear volume, whereas the stated unit mm3/(N·m) is a normalized wear rate rather than wear volume.
